To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a new BRCA1 mutation, which seems to be a Tunisian founder, in a high proportion of hereditary cases.
the prevalence of deleterious BRCA1 mutations among Tunisian breast cancer families is 37.5% and that one mutation (c.798_799 delTT) seems to be a Tunisian founder.
(1) the prevalence of deleterious BRCA1 mutations is high among Tunisian breast cancer families; (2) the c.798 + 799delTT (c.916 + 917delTT) mutation is a Tunisain founder mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most frequent mutations in the BRCA1 gene in the Tunisian high-risk families, the analysis of their distribution and the determination of their founder status.
the identification of BRCA1 founder mutations in Tunisian breast cancer families and their contribution to the genetic susceptibility to breast cancer in the Tunisian populations.
the genetic characterization of BRCA1 gene mutations in Tunisian hereditary breast cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BRCA1 mutation prevalence in the Tunisian breast cancer population is similar to that of other ethnic groups.
BRCA1 mutations are frequent in the Tunisian hereditary breast cancer and should be considered in genetic counselling of high-risk breast cancer women in the Tunisian and North African populations.
the BRCA1 mutation spectrum in the Tunisian breast cancer population is heterogeneous and that the prevalence of BRCA1 germline mutations varies between 20 and 40%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of BRCA1 mutation in the Tunisian breast cancer population is 10.3%.
BRCA1 mutations account for a substantial proportion of hereditary cases of breast cancer in Tunisia and that a founder mutation is present in the Tunisian breast cancer families.

37.5% of Tunisian breast cancer families carry deleterious BRCA1 mutations and the c.798 + 799delTT (p.Glu267ArgfsX2) mutation is the most frequent one, occurring in three unrelated Tunisian families and is associated with a common founder haplotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that

genetic testing of BRCA1 should be offered to Tunisian breast/ovarian cancer families, and that the BRCA1 mutation spectrum in the Tunisian and other Middle Eastern and North Africa populations should be further characterized.
the contribution of BRCA 1 mutations to heredity breast cancer in the Middle East and Africa is underestimated.
BRCA1 testing in Tunisian families is highly recommended.
